topic: Federated learning for privacy-preserving clinical decision support in hospital networks
final_review: The application of federated learning in hospital networks has gained significant attention in recent years, particularly in the context of clinical decision support (Rieke et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2020). Federated learning enables the training of machine learning models on decentralized data, ensuring the preservation of patient privacy (Torkzadehmahani et al., 2022; Kaissis et al., 2020). This approach has been explored in various medical imaging applications, including radiomics, which bridges the gap between medical imaging and personalized medicine (Lambin et al., 2017; Castiglioni et al., 2021). The integration of federated learning with other technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), has also been investigated (Al‐Fuqaha et al., 2015; Boobalan et al., 2022). This fusion has the potential to enhance the security and efficiency of clinical decision support systems (Sirohi et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2025). Furthermore, the use of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques can improve the transparency and accountability of these systems (Barredo Arrieta et al., 2019). Despite the promising results, there are still several challenges and research gaps in the field. For instance, the lack of standardization in federated learning protocols and the need for more robust evaluation metrics have been highlighted (Chamani Shiranthika et al., 2023; Miotto et al., 2017). Additionally, the application of federated learning in cancer diagnostics and treatment has shown great potential, but more research is needed to fully explore its capabilities (Tiwari et al., 2025). In terms of agreements and contradictions, most studies concur on the benefits of federated learning in preserving patient privacy and enhancing clinical decision support (Rieke et al., 2020; Torkzadehmahani et al., 2022). However, some studies have raised concerns about the potential risks and challenges associated with the implementation of federated learning in real-world healthcare settings (Xu et al., 2020; Kaissis et al., 2020). In conclusion, federated learning has the potential to revolutionize clinical decision support in hospital networks, particularly in the context of medical imaging and personalized medicine. However, further research is needed to address the existing challenges and gaps in the field. References: Al‐Fuqaha, A., Guizani, M., & Mohammadi, M. (2015).
